summary: Validate and temporarily pause aggressive per-tenant batching/cache/quant profiles; provide traffic-split mitigation and safe restore
description:
Issue summary: Customer BrightHealth AI reports recurring 95p latency spikes after we applied an aggressive per-tenant optimization bundle (large batch size + KV prefetch + int8-like quant profile). Impact: High - production traffic sees repeated 95th/99th percentile tail latency > 1.2s causing downstream request timeouts and a customer SLA alert. They want a low-risk way to pause the tenant's optimization set, shift a small percentage of traffic to a stable profile, and then validate behavior before a full restore.

We need support-run commands and an ordered playbook that avoids mass restart or global config changes. Customer prefers zero downtime for most users; willing to accept a small controlled traffic split.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Tenant BrightHealth AI configured optimizer profile: batching.max_tokens=1024, batching.preferred_batch_size=64, kv_prefetch=true, quant_profile=fast-approx-v2

2) Synthetic load: 120 concurrent users, median request length ~ 120 tokens, intermittent long-context sessions (up to 1024),
   observe tail latency over 95th percentile on production route redwood-api/v1/generate
3) Monitor: console -> routes -> redwood-api/v1/generate -> 95p/99p latency spikes correlated with increased batch construction time and elevated GPU busy-waits
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: aggressive batching combined with kv_prefetch is increasing queueing latency under bursty arrival patterns; quant_profile fast-approx-v2 may increase compute jitter on certain sequence lengths.
Observed: increases in batch formation time when request arrival bursts are > expected inter-arrival time. KV hit rate dropped ~12% during spikes (suspected misaligned prefix caching keys).
Router traces show several requests delayed in batching layer for 40-80ms while waiting for batch completion before GPU dispatch - amplifies under N:1 request patterns (long-running contexts).
No 5xx errors; error rates stable. No node-level OOM. Dedicated pool utilization at 78% but queue length variance high during spikes.
proposed_mitigation_playbook: 1) Capture current optimizer profile snapshot for tenant (console export + s3 archive): command provided to customer for audit.

2) 'Soft-pause' per-tenant optimizations by disabling batching.max_wait_ms and kv_prefetch only for that tenant (no global rollout). This should be toggled via the tenant gating API to avoid node restarts.
3) Apply a 10% traffic split rule: route 90% to current profile, 10% to 'stable' profile (smaller batch size, kv_prefetch=false, quant_profile=latency-safe). Observe 5/15/95/99p for 30 minutes.
4) If metrics improve for the 10% bucket, increase split gradually (25% -> 50% -> 100%) with monitoring checks at each step. If any regression observed, revert split to previous ratio.

5) When back at 100% stable profile, run a controlled A/B test to reintroduce individual optimizations (first kv_prefetch as a toggle, then quant_profile change), verifying KV hit rate and tail latency after each step.
6) Provide customer-facing commands and a console checklist for performing the toggles without support intervention.
7) Post-mitigation: collect traces and schedule a design follow-up to refine batching heuristics (e.g., adaptive batch size based on observed inter-arrival distribution).
risk_assessment: Soft-pause (disabling kv_prefetch and adjusting batching wait) is low risk: per-tenant flag toggles are applied at request-router layer, no pod restarts required.
Traffic-splitting increases complexity for a short window; must ensure idempotent routing rules and avoid sticky sessions that bypass split.
Quant profile rollback might change token-level costs slightly (higher compute cost) — inform billing/sales if long duration.
If KV cache keys are misaligned, toggling kv_prefetch could temporarily drop hit rate until cache warms; include warming phase in playbook.
comments: Asha Patel (2026-03-10): Customer filed initial request after two incidents where 95p latency exceeded SLA. They requested a non-disruptive mitigation path and checklist.

Marcus Lee (2026-03-11): Confirmed tenant's optimizer snapshot exists (s3://redwood-backups/brighthealth/optimizers/2026-03-09.json). Drafted stepwise soft-pause commands and test traffic-split rule. Assigned to on-call SRE for execution window.

Elena Gomez (SRE) (2026-03-12): Executed 10% traffic split at 02:20 UTC. 10% bucket (stable profile) 95p dropped from 1.25s -> 360ms. 90% bucket still saw spikes. Recommended progressive ramp after 30m steady-state.
Customer Rep - Tom Rivera (BrightHealth) (2026-03-12): Approved 10% test; requests that we avoid full quant profile rollback due to latency-sensitive models for some endpoints.
Marcus Lee (2026-03-13): Increased split to 50% after stable metrics. No errors observed. Preparing final rollback and restore checklist.
Finance Notice (2026-03-13): Potential compute cost increase during stable-profile period flagged to finance; customer notified.
resolution: Implemented soft-pause for batching.max_wait_ms and disabled kv_prefetch for BrightHealth tenant via tenant-gating API; applied progressive traffic-split to stable profile, validated improved 95p/99p latency, and retained stable profile after customer sign-off. Quant profile change was deferred and will be re-evaluated with extended A/B testing. Archived optimizer snapshot to S3 and updated customer's runbook with step-by-step commands and confirmation checks.
follow_up_tasks: 1) Engineering: Add a console 'soft-pause' one-click toggle and safe-restore wizard for per-tenant optimizer profiles (owner: runtime team, due: 2026-04-06).
2) Product: Review default batching heuristics and consider a conservative tenant guardrail for newly onboarded profiles (owner: product, due: 2026-04-15).
3) Support: Publish KB article 'How to safely split traffic and soft-pause tenant optimizer settings' and attach to BrightHealth account (owner: support docs, due: 2026-03-20).
4) SRE: Implement automated metric checks to detect KV hit-rate drops >= 10% concurrent with tail-latency regressions (owner: SRE, due: 2026-03-28).
